thesis: August 7 was a concentrated loss session: all four positions lost INR 2,480.40 net, led by three newly enlarged Rangebound positions losing INR 1,830.08. The strongest recurring improvement is to delay Rangebound entry from 10:00 to 10:30 IST; the pre-10:30 subgroup is consistently weak while later entries are positive in aggregate. Fresh Breakout also remains structurally negative and now warrants a medium-confidence pause. Reducing Rangebound exposure from INR 200,000 to INR 100,000 is prudent risk containment but has low confidence because only one session used the new cap.

selectedDay.setupSummary: Three Rangebound positions lost INR 1,830.08 net and the one Fresh Breakout position lost INR 650.32 net.
selectedDay.exitSummary: Two confirmed-stop exits lost INR 1,639.94, one VWAP-loss exit lost INR 656.16, and one momentum-deterioration exit lost INR 184.30. No trade reached a target or trailing-profit exit.

rangebound: KPITTECH entered near INR 199,884 exposure and lost INR 989.62 on a confirmed stop after 19.9 minutes.
INTELLECT entered near INR 199,879 exposure and lost INR 656.16 on a VWAP-loss exit after 39.9 minutes.
GODREJPROP entered near INR 199,025 exposure and lost INR 184.30 on signal deterioration after 45 minutes.
All three Rangebound positions opened before 10:30 IST. Their losses therefore support the entry-time diagnosis independently of the later exit type.
dailyDiagnosis.freshBreakout: UNIONBANK entered at INR 99,896 exposure with score 80 and decision score 76.5, then lost INR 650.32 on a confirmed stop. Raising the Fresh Breakout score floor would not have blocked this trade.
dailyDiagnosis.exitControls: The shared 75-minute no-progress window did not cause today's losses: every position exited within 45 minutes through stop, VWAP, or momentum rules. SIMULATION_RUNNER_INITIAL_STOP_PCT is also irrelevant because no Momentum Runner traded.

opportunityLossAnalysis.scope: Sell candidates that did not become trades, evaluated across the seven requested sessions without Replay, backtest, sweep, or live-setting mutation.

dominantBlockers: 2,881 rows: completed confirmation candle was not bearish.
1,929 rows: decision score was 54 versus the configured minimum of 70.
1,402 rows: entry state was still Wait.
1,282 rows: entry state was Near trigger.
620 rows: late-short acceleration had only 1 of 4 required confirmations.
523 rows: bearish entry conflicted with the sector or market regime.

exactConfigCheck.method: Static sole-blocker re-evaluation at the exact proposed value, one date-symbol observation per session, excluding symbols already traded short; modeled to stored day close at INR 100,000 exposure after Zerodha charges and 0.06% slippage.
exactConfigCheck.decision: Preserve the current 0.30% cap. The modeled INR 592.61 opportunity is only three candidates across two dates, while the four shorts actually admitted under current rules on August 5-6 all lost INR 1,218.54 net in aggregate.

otherConfigChecks: Reducing SIMULATION_SHORT_CONFIRM_BARS from 2 to 1 would not solve the dominant non-bearish-candle rejection because bearish completed-candle direction, closes below trigger and VWAP, wick quality, live holds, and fresh volume remain independent requirements.
Disabling SIMULATION_SHORT_REQUIRE_COMPLETED_CANDLE would remove a materially important confirmation safeguard and is not supported by the available multi-date evidence.

limitations: This result is analytics-reviewed only. No Replay, backtest, sweep, targeted settings trial, or setting application was run.

August 7 has 196 snapshots, 187 usable snapshots, 27,355 candidate rows, 24,940 actionable rows, and one settings fingerprint. Repeated snapshot appearances were not treated as independent observations.
Only three positions on one date used approximately INR 200,000 Rangebound exposure, so the exact INR 100,000 sizing recommendation has low confidence.

The INR 100,000 sizing comparison holds today's symbols, entries, exits, and exit-leg proportions constant and recalculates Zerodha charges. It does not model different queue position, slippage, liquidity, or capacity-driven selection.
Entry-time admission metrics are newly persisted; older dates do not consistently contain every Rangebound lower-distance, cost, and live-depth field needed to isolate additional quality gates.
The Rangebound time and exposure recommendations overlap on today's three trades. Their combined result has not been evaluated and they should not be treated as a validated package.

recommendations.description: Earliest IST minute when a rangebound setup may open a new position.
recommendations.rationale: Delay Rangebound entries from 10:00 to 10:30 IST because the opening subgroup is persistently loss-making while later entries remain profitable in aggregate.
evidence: Affected group: 18 Rangebound positions opened before 10:30 across 5 dates; 4 wins, INR -1,417.36 gross, INR 1,133.19 charges, INR -2,550.55 net, and profit factor 0.27.
Four of five affected dates support the delay: July 31 INR -76.92, August 4 INR -84.90, August 6 INR -583.90, and August 7 INR -1,830.08. August 3 contradicts with INR 25.25 net.
Unaffected group: 27 Rangebound positions opened at or after 10:30 across 5 dates; 11 wins, INR 1,896.39 gross, INR 1,379.66 charges, INR 516.73 net, and profit factor 1.20.
All three August 7 Rangebound positions opened before 10:30 and all lost, across three distinct exit mechanisms: stop, VWAP, and momentum deterioration.
Total relevant setup population: 45 Rangebound positions across 6 dates, INR -2,033.82 net, and profit factor 0.67.
recommendations.risk: The later start would reject four profitable early Rangebound trades and could miss genuine opening reversions. August 3 is a contradictory positive date, and observational timing does not prove that rejected capital would be redeployed profitably.

validation.reason: Medium confidence: the exact time filter affects 18 transactions across 5 dates, aggregate evidence is favorable, and 4 of 5 relevant dates support it. The sample is below the 20-transaction high-confidence threshold and one date contradicts.

recommendations.description: Allows Fresh Breakout candidates to open new simulation trades.
recommendations.rationale: Pause Fresh Breakout entries because losses persist across scores and exit types, including today's high-score UNIONBANK stop, so another score-floor increase is unlikely to address the setup-wide weakness.
evidence: Affected group: all 12 Fresh Breakout positions across 4 dates; 1 win, INR -2,025.82 gross, INR 921.33 charges, INR -2,947.15 net, and profit factor 0.31.
Three of four relevant dates support pausing: August 3 INR -1,424.58, August 6 INR -1,249.07, and August 7 INR -650.32. July 31 contradicts with INR 376.82 net.
The only winner was GAIL at INR 1,307.46 net; the other 11 positions lost, including score-80 UNIONBANK and score-88 DIXON, so weakness is not confined to the low-score band.
Unaffected group: the other 67 positions produced INR 1,628.42 gross, INR 3,926.48 charges, and INR -2,298.06 net.
The seven-session portfolio has INR -5,245.21 net PnL and profit factor 0.65; Fresh Breakout accounts for 56% of the aggregate net loss.
recommendations.risk: Pausing removes the exceptional GAIL winner and any future breakout recovery. The setup has transactions on only four dates, and disabling it does not repair the remaining portfolio's negative expectancy.

validation.reason: Medium confidence: 12 affected transactions across 4 dates meet the medium sample threshold, aggregate evidence favors pausing, and 3 of 4 relevant dates support it. One large winning outlier and limited date coverage prevent high confidence.

recommendations.description: Maximum rupee exposure allowed for one Rangebound position without increasing the shared cap for other setups.
recommendations.rationale: Reduce the new Rangebound cap to INR 100,000 as risk containment after all three approximately INR 200,000 entries lost on their first observed session.
evidence: Affected observed group: 3 approximately INR 200,000 Rangebound positions on August 7; 0 wins, INR -1,476.45 gross, INR 353.63 charges, INR -1,830.08 net, and profit factor 0.
A fixed-price INR 100,000 arithmetic comparison for the same three positions produces INR -983.63 modeled net, reducing the observed loss by INR 846.45 while leaving every trade unprofitable.

The three entries consumed about INR 598,789 of gross exposure. At INR 100,000 each they would consume about INR 300,000, leaving substantially more room below the INR 800,000 portfolio gross-exposure ceiling.
Unaffected historical Rangebound group: 42 smaller positions across 5 dates; 15 wins, INR 1,955.48 gross, INR 2,159.22 charges, INR -203.74 net, and profit factor 0.95.
Only August 7 contains direct INR 200,000 exposure evidence; the other six requested dates cannot support or contradict the exact cap change.
recommendations.risk: The recommendation is based on only three trades from one session. Lower exposure increases charges as a percentage of notional and may reduce gains when Rangebound performance improves. The fixed-price comparison is not an executable counterfactual and does not model different liquidity or trade selection.

validation.reason: Low confidence because only 3 affected positions on 1 date directly used the INR 200,000 cap. The observed loss supports immediate risk containment, but the exact INR 100,000 alternative is not replay-tested or validated.
